blocks.content: Jurisdiction defines the legal authority of a court to hear and decide cases under the Constitution of India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Exclusive original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court extends to federal disputes between the Union and States or among States.
Writ jurisdiction under Article 32 is a Fundamental Right, whereas under Article 226 it is a constitutional remedy with wider scope.
Appellate jurisdiction covers constitutional, civil, and criminal matters coming from High Courts.
Advisory jurisdiction under Article 143 empowers the President to consult the Supreme Court on questions of law or public importance.
High Courts have broader writ jurisdiction than the Supreme Court because Art 226 covers legal rights in addition to fundamental rights.
An advisory opinion given by the Supreme Court under Article 143 is not binding on the President.
Federal disputes between Centre and States fall strictly under the exclusive original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
